analysis.title: Weekly HF Highlights: HF De-Grossing Persists Amidst Continued AI Weakness
key_insights: HFs kept unwinding gross exposure on both long and short books this week. The pace accelerated into Thursday Oct 22, when the US L/S Momentum pair (MSZZMOMO) fell 7.9%, its worst day in 3 years, amid weakness in AI Infrastructure trades.
The roughly 2-week unwind in N. America amounts to -1.8% of gross exposure, slightly short of the July unwind (-2.1%). L/S strategies have cut nearly 6% of US gross exposure since the end of June.
US L/S gross leverage rose to 210% (94th percentile since 2010) despite active de-grossing. PnL losses eroded equity faster than HFs cut positions, so gross relative to equity rose mechanically.

US L/S net leverage fell to 47% (25th percentile since 2010) after briefly touching 50% mid-week, near the lowest of the last 12 months. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell about 2% over the week, because long reductions were concentrated in higher-beta AI trades.

Net exposure to the AI Infrastructure trade (MSXXAI Index) is now in line with its R3K weight, down from about 5% overweight at the start of October. The theme is still about 35% of US HF net exposure and remains a main driver of HF PnL.

Software net exposure keeps recovering from lows, with long demand in Infra Software (MSXXINSW) and Cybersecurity (MSXXCYBR). Health Care saw long additions after the recent de-grossing, and HFs covered shorts in Consumer Discretionary.

De-grossing was global. In APAC, selling was concentrated in Taiwan on continued Tech unwinds, and China also contributed with broad-based supply. In Europe it was driven mostly by short covers, with a smaller amount of long selling.

In Europe, US-based HFs drove the short covering and EU-based HFs drove the long selling. Long reductions were concentrated in EU Industrials, Energy and Banks. Short covers were concentrated in Consumer and TMT (EU Software, EU AI Disrupted Names).

Thursday was a near-record loss day (95th percentile) for global long portfolios. The average global L/S fund lost 73bps this week against MSCI down 54bps, and the average US-based L/S fund lost 33bps, all on Thursday.
MTD, the average global L/S fund is down 2% and the average US-based L/S fund is down 2.6%. YTD, global L/S is up 5.1% (median +3.28%) and US L/S is up 6.4%, versus gains of about 15% ahead of July.
EU-based L/S funds are up 2.4% YTD against SXXP +10.8%. Asia-based L/S funds are up 4% YTD against MSCI Asia +15.8%.
Top 50 crowded longs minus shorts fell 2.0% WTD and 5.1% MTD, and are up 16.8% YTD. The N. America top 50 longs fell 3.27% on Oct 22 against the S&P 500 TR at -1.21%.

sector_views.rationale: HF net exposure is recovering from lows on long demand in Infra Software and Cybersecurity.
Long additions began emerging after the recent de-grossing episode.
HFs unwound shorts in the US this week.

risk_factors: Further de-grossing in AI Infrastructure and crowded longs could extend losses in high-beta names.
Momentum factor unwinds, as on Oct 22 (MSZZMOMO -7.9%), hit crowded long portfolios.
US gross leverage at the 94th percentile leaves HFs exposed to further mechanical deleveraging if PnL losses continue.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S gross leverage is 210% (+3% WoW, 94th percentile since 2010, 80th percentile over 5 years). US L/S net leverage is 47% (-1% WoW, 25th percentile since 2010, 2nd percentile over 1 year).
Europe gross leverage is 179% (+4% WoW, 94th percentile over 1 year) and net is 50% (-3% WoW). Asia gross is 126% (0% WoW) and net is 53% (-4% WoW, -10% MTD).
The US L/S Momentum pair (MSZZMOMO) fell 7.9% on Oct 22, its worst day in 3 years.
Top 50 crowded longs minus shorts: WTD -2.04% spread, MTD -5.12%, YTD +16.77%. In N. America the top 50 longs are -6.59% MTD and +28.39% YTD against the S&P 500 TR at +0.20% MTD.
In Asia, the top 50 longs are -12.94% MTD and the shorts -6.31% MTD, a -6.64% spread.
The AI Infrastructure theme (MSXXAI) is about 35% of US HF net exposure, down from about 5% overweight vs the R3K at the start of October to a neutral weight.
